LanguageData.SimpleFarming_DebugLoggingHint: Logs the full husbandry calculation for each animal the first time its info card is opened, plus any animals the mod had to skip. Prefixed [SimpleFarming] in the log (dev mode console).
LanguageData.SimpleFarming_AwakeHoursLabel: Hours per day animals seek mates
LanguageData.SimpleFarming_AwakeHoursHint: Animals only look for mates while awake (roughly 16 of 24 hours). This feeds the pregnancy-speed and male-ratio math. Keep at 16 unless you know better.
LanguageData.SF_HerdFoodLabel: food per female per day (incl. males)
LanguageData.SF_NetPerDayLabel: net meat per female per day
LanguageData.SF_SlaughterPregnantValue: yes - litter not worth the feed
LanguageData.SF_RatioTipMammal:
A male looks for a fertile female about once every {0} hours while awake ({1} h per day), so roughly {2} mating attempts per day. Each mating impregnates with a {3} chance.

One male therefore impregnates about {4} females per day. With a {5}-day gestation that keeps {6} females pregnant back-to-back - the ratio shown.

Caveats: males only search a short radius for females, so keep the herd together; males also spend time eating and wandering. Round up when in doubt - a spare male eats little, a missing male stalls the whole herd.
LanguageData.SF_RatioBreedingOnlyNote: This animal also lays edible unfertilized eggs without any males. The ratio above only matters when you want the eggs to hatch.
LanguageData.SF_MalesForEggsTip: Unfertilized egg progress stops partway ({0}%), so without a male this animal never lays at all. With the recommended male ratio the average fertilization wait is about {1} days per clutch.
LanguageData.SF_TimeToPregnancyTip: A freshly fertile female conceives after about {0} days on average when males are around: {1} mating attempts per male per day, each impregnating with a {2} chance.\n\nThis wait is included in the reproduction cycle, the offspring rate and all food-efficiency numbers below.
LanguageData.SF_TimeToFertilizationTip: A female's next clutch is fertilized after about {0} days on average when males are around ({1} mating attempts per male per day, fertilization is guaranteed on mating).\n\nOnly stall-layers lose laying time waiting; layers that can lay unfertilized eggs lose nothing.
LanguageData.SF_CycleTipMammal: Gestation {0} days plus {1} days average conception wait makes {2} days per litter of {3}.
LanguageData.SF_CycleTipEgg: One clutch of {0} eggs every {1} days{2}.
LanguageData.SF_CycleStallNote: , plus about {0} days waiting for fertilization
LanguageData.SF_HatchTip: Fertilized eggs hatch after {0} days. Eggs don't eat, so this delays offspring but costs no food.
LanguageData.SF_OffspringPerDayTipMammal: A litter of {0} every {1} days of gestation ({2} days including the average conception wait) gives {3} offspring per female per day with ample males.
LanguageData.SF_OffspringPerDayTipEgg: {0} eggs per clutch, one clutch every {1} days ({2} days including the average fertilization wait) gives {3} hatchlings per female per day with ample males.
LanguageData.SF_MeatPerDayTip: Growing the offspring to adults and slaughtering them yields {0} meat nutrition per female per day ({1} offspring/day x {2} nutrition each) - before subtracting their growth food, and before the females' and males' own upkeep.\n\nMilk, wool, edible eggs and leather are extra on top of this.
LanguageData.SF_LeatherPerDayTip: The same slaughter also yields {0}: {1} units per grown adult, or {2} units per female per day at the offspring rate above (same grown-adult basis as the meat row).\n\nLeather scales with the slaughter stage's body size factor and is a bonus on top of the meat numbers - it is not counted in any nutrition efficiency or the net row.
LanguageData.SF_HerdFoodTip:
A female eats {0} nutrition per day of the assumed feed; adding her share of breeding males ({1} per female) gives {2} nutrition per female per day of breeding-stock upkeep (raw nutrition).
Offspring food is counted separately, per animal grown.
LanguageData.SF_AdultMeatNutritionTip:
{0} units of meat x {1} nutrition each = {2} nutrition from a cleanly slaughtered adult.

Leather: {3} units (not counted as food anywhere in this block).
Animals killed by damage instead of careful slaughter yield only 66% meat and leather.
LanguageData.SF_EfficiencyTip:
Slaughter as {0}, herd fed {1} (x{2} over raw food):
- meat returned: {3} nutrition ({11}) - food spent per offspring (raw nutrition of that feed): {4} - {5} mother's gestation food - {6} mother's conception-wait food - {7} own growth food to this stage - {8} fathers' share
Efficiency: {3} / {4} = {9}. Above 100% the animal returns more food than the operation spends on it.
Excluding the fathers' share, the same slaughter returns {10}.
LanguageData.SF_RecommendedTip: {0}\n\nSlaughter age with the best all-in nutrition return per food spent (parents' and offspring's food, fathers included). Cheaper food (grazing) or extra products (milk, wool, leather, eggs) can shift the real answer.
LanguageData.SF_PregnantAdviceLet: Let her give birth - the litter outvalues the remaining pregnancy feed. Letting offspring grow past birth only pays if the grown-stage efficiency above exceeds 100%.
LanguageData.SF_PregnantAdviceSlaughter: Slaughtering now is fine - the litter does not outvalue the remaining pregnancy feed.
LanguageData.SF_NetEggsNote: For eggs instead of meat: an unfertilized-egg pen needs no males at all - {0}/day of hen upkeep vs {1}/day of egg nutrition, without hatching or butchering work.
LanguageData.SF_DifficultyYieldNote: Your difficulty's butcher yield x{0} is included.
LanguageData.SF_CurveNote: The game's meat post-processing boosts small yields (minimum ~14 meat before body-size scaling tapers off at 40), so small life stages return more meat than a straight body-size proportion of the adult - exactly what butchering yields in game.
LanguageData.SF_FeedAssumed: Herd feed assumed: {0} (x{1} over raw food) - the best feed this animal's diet and stomach allow. Feed raw pieces instead and every food number scales back up accordingly.
LanguageData.SimpleFarming_FeedChoiceHeader: Feeds considered for the assumed herd feed
LanguageData.SimpleFarming_FeedMeals: Consider simple meals (up to x1.80 - only if the stomach fits a whole 0.9 meal)
LanguageData.SimpleFarming_FeedChoiceHint: The block assumes the herd is fed on the best ENABLED feed the animal can eat; raw pieces (x1.00) are always the fallback baseline. Defaults: raw pieces + simple meals. Changes apply immediately.
